lessons.objective: 1. être · Identifying a new group: Use être to identify people, describe a group, give origin and say where an event takes place.

lessons.title: 2. avoir · What exists and what is finished
lessons.objective: 2. avoir · What exists and what is finished: Use il y a to say that something exists; it never changes, whether the noun is singular or plural, and the negative is il n'y a pas de.
lessons.explanation:
Use il y a to say that something exists; it never changes, whether the noun is singular or plural, and the negative is il n'y a pas de. Avoir + past participle forms the passé composé, and the participle does not agree with the subject.
Il y a deux dossiers pour chaque personne. — There are two folders for each person.
Il n'y a pas assez de stylos. — There are not enough pens.

lessons.title: 4. pouvoir · Ability and permission in a new place
lessons.objective: 4. pouvoir · Ability and permission in a new place: Use pouvoir + infinitive for ability, possibility and permission.
lessons.explanation:

lessons.title: 7. dire · Passing on words accurately
lessons.objective: 7. dire · Passing on words accurately: Use dire: je dis, nous disons, vous dites, ils disent; the participle is dit.
lessons.explanation:
Use dire: je dis, nous disons, vous dites, ils disent; the participle is dit. Dire que + indicative reports words, and dire à quelqu'un de + infinitive passes on an instruction.
La directrice dit qu'elle est en route. — The director says she is on her way.
Je dis à mes collègues d'attendre ici. — I tell my colleagues to wait here.

lessons.objective: 56. supposer · Assuming and what something entails: Supposer is a regular -er verb built on poser (je suppose, nous supposons), and je suppose que takes the indicative.

lessons.title: 60. perdre · Losing an item, missing transport and wasting time
lessons.objective: 60. perdre · Losing an item, missing transport and wasting time: Perdre (je perds, nous perdons; participle perdu) means to lose something and to waste time (perdre du temps à + infinitive); se perdre means to get lost.
lessons.explanation:
Perdre (je perds, nous perdons; participle perdu) means to lose something and to waste time (perdre du temps à + infinitive); se perdre means to get lost. Missing a bus or a train is rater or manquer, never perdre.
Parfois, je perds du temps à chercher d'anciens messages. — Sometimes I waste time looking for old messages.
Hier, j'ai perdu la copie dont j'avais besoin. — Yesterday I lost the copy I needed.
